questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A speech delivered without any preparation"
questions.explanation: The word is "extempore": spoken or done without preparation. Do not confuse it with "monologue": a long speech by one person in a conversation or play.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "That which cannot be read because it is badly written"
questions.explanation: The word is "illegible": not clear enough to be read. Do not confuse it with "inaudible": not loud enough to be heard.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A person or habit that cannot be corrected"
questions.explanation: The word is "incorrigible": not able to be corrected or reformed. Do not confuse it with "incurable": not able to be healed of a disease.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "That which cannot be avoided"
questions.explanation: The word is "inevitable": certain to happen; unavoidable. Do not confuse it with "incredible": too extraordinary to be believed.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "Government by a small group of people"
questions.explanation: The word is "oligarchy": rule by a few. Do not confuse it with "democracy": rule by the people through elected representatives.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "Present everywhere at the same time"
questions.explanation: The word is "omnipresent": present in all places at once. Do not confuse it with "omniscient": knowing everything.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The killing of a king"
questions.explanation: The word is "regicide": the act of killing a king. Do not confuse it with "fratricide": the killing of one's brother.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A large cage or house in which birds are kept"
questions.explanation: The word is "aviary": a place where birds are kept. Do not confuse it with "apiary": a place where bees are kept.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A system of government carried out by officials who are not elected"
questions.explanation: The word is "bureaucracy": administration by appointed officials. Do not confuse it with "autocracy": rule by one person with absolute power.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "Something that can never be satisfied"
questions.explanation: The word is "insatiable": impossible to satisfy. Do not confuse it with "insolvent": unable to pay one's debts.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The life story of a person written by that person"
questions.explanation: The word is "autobiography": a person's life story written by himself or herself. Do not confuse it with "biography": a life story written by someone else.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A home or centre that cares for the terminally ill"
questions.explanation: The word is "hospice": a place caring for the dying. Do not confuse it with "hospital": an institution for treating the sick and injured generally.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A speech by one character alone on the stage speaking his thoughts aloud"
questions.explanation: The word is "soliloquy": speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone, especially in a play. Do not confuse it with "monologue": a long speech by one person addressed to others.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "Fit to be eaten"
questions.explanation: The word is "edible": safe and fit to be eaten. Do not confuse it with "eligible": qualified to be chosen.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A person who is unable to pay his debts"
questions.explanation: The word is "insolvent": unable to pay one's debts. Do not confuse it with "insomniac": a person who cannot sleep.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A remedy for all diseases"
questions.explanation: The word is "panacea": a cure for all ills. Do not confuse it with "antidote": a medicine that counteracts a poison.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A substance that counteracts the effect of a poison"
questions.explanation: The word is "antidote": a remedy that works against a poison. Do not confuse it with "panacea": a supposed cure for all diseases.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "One who knows everything"
questions.explanation: The word is "omniscient": all-knowing. Do not confuse it with "omnipresent": present everywhere.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The killing of one's own father"
questions.explanation: The word is "patricide": the act of killing one's father. Do not confuse it with "matricide": the killing of one's mother.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "The killing of one's own brother or sister"
questions.explanation: The word is "fratricide": the act of killing a brother or sister. Do not confuse it with "patricide": the killing of one's father.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "Lasting for a very short time"
questions.explanation: The word is "ephemeral": short-lived. Do not confuse it with "eternal": lasting forever.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A fixed sum of money paid regularly to a person after retirement"
questions.explanation: The word is "pension": a regular payment made to a retired person. Do not confuse it with "pittance": a very small amount of money.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A building where grain is stored"
questions.explanation: The word is "granary": a storehouse for grain. Do not confuse it with "armoury": a place where weapons are stored.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "Done of one's own free will"
questions.explanation: The word is "voluntary": done by choice, not by compulsion. Do not confuse it with "compulsory": required by rule.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "That which cannot be seen"
questions.explanation: The word is "invisible": unable to be seen. Do not confuse it with "inaudible": unable to be heard.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "That which cannot be heard"
questions.explanation: The word is "inaudible": unable to be heard. Do not confuse it with "invisible": unable to be seen.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A person who has personally seen a crime or accident and can testify about it"
questions.explanation: The word is "eyewitness": a person who has personally seen an event, especially a crime or accident. Do not confuse it with "accomplice": a person who helps another commit a crime.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A handwriting that is difficult to read or a document that cannot be understood"
questions.explanation: The word is "indecipherable": impossible to read or understand. Do not confuse it with "illiterate": unable to read or write.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A person who leaves his country to live permanently in another"
questions.explanation: The word is "emigrant": a person who leaves his own country to settle elsewhere. Do not confuse it with "immigrant": a person who comes into a country to settle there.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A medicine or treatment that prevents the occurrence of a disease"
questions.explanation: The word is "preventive": intended to stop something from happening. Do not confuse it with "curative": intended to heal an existing illness.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A person who comes to settle permanently in a foreign country"
questions.explanation: The word is "immigrant": a person who comes to live permanently in another country. Do not confuse it with "emigrant": a person who leaves his own country to settle elsewhere.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A place where dead bodies are kept before burial or cremation"
questions.explanation: The word is "mortuary": a place where dead bodies are kept temporarily. Do not confuse it with "cemetery": a place where bodies are buried.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A school or institution where children without parents are looked after"
questions.explanation: The word is "orphanage": an institution caring for children without parents. Do not confuse it with "hospice": a home caring for the terminally ill.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A medicine that relieves pain without curing the disease"
questions.explanation: The word is "palliative": easing pain or a problem without removing its cause. Do not confuse it with "preventive": stopping something from happening.
